Kyrgios, who had been ​provisionally suspended since August 4, had ‌entered into a treatment programme approved by the International Tennis Integrity Agency (ITIA) to ​reduce the three-month default suspension under WADA rules. The Australian gave a sample at an ATP tournament in Majorca in June which tested positive for benzoylecgonine, a metabolite of cocaine. messages.text: FIFA accuses UEFA of launching 'smear campaign' against Infantino

metadata.summary: FIFA has accused European football’s governing body of launching a “smear campaign” against Gianni Infantino in a challenge to legal action over the aborted attempt to sell part of the World Cup to private investors.
metadata.content: Gianni Infantino latest: FIFA accuses UEFA of launching a 'smear campaign' after legal cases filed in American courts | Football News | Sky Sports Skip to content Gianni Infantino latest: FIFA accuses UEFA of launching a 'smear campaign' after legal cases filed in American courts UEFA has warned it is considering launching criminal proceedings against Mr Infantino in Switzerland, where FIFA has its headquarters, and has filed legal cases in American courts. Rob Harris Sports correspondent, Sky News Friday 4 September 2026 07:06, UK Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player UEFA has warned it is considering launching criminal proceedings against Gianni Infantino in Switzerland, where FIFA has its headquarters, and has filed legal cases in American courts. FIFA has accused European football’s governing body of launching a “smear campaign” against Gianni Infantino in a challenge to legal action over the aborted attempt to sell part of the World Cup to private investors. UEFA has filed legal cases in American courts seeking evidence relating to the controversial venture and warned it is considering launching criminal proceedings against Mr Infantino in Switzerland where FIFA has its headquarters. FIFA has now filed a response in a New York court, saying: "While these applications are styled as legal pleadings with captions and docket numbers, they are little more than press releases in further support of UEFA's smear campaign against FIFA and its leadership." But the seamer was rewarded for simplicity on Thursday as a five-wicket haul - her first in international cricket - helped her side wrap up an one-day international series win over Ireland. Prioritising the wobble-seam delivery that angled in to the right handers, Wong bowled opposition captain Gaby Lewis through the gate for her first strike of the day. messages.text: Bradford snap seven-match losing streak with win over Castleford

metadata.summary: A five-try first half display by Bradford Bulls helped snap a seven-match losing streak with a 32-22 victory over Castleford Tigers.
metadata.content: Super League: Bradford Bulls produce five-try first half to snap seven-match losing streak with win over Castleford Tigers | Rugby League News | Sky Sports Skip to content Super League: Bradford Bulls produce five-try first half to snap seven-match losing streak with win over Castleford Tigers Bradford Bulls snapped a seven-match losing streak with a 32-22 win over Castleford Tigers; Sky Sports will show every Super League game live this season, including two matches each round exclusively live, while the remaining five matches will be broadcast on Sky Sports+ Thursday 3 September 2026 22:40, UK Image: Dean scored a try as the Bulls broke their losing streak A five-try first half display by Bradford Bulls helped snap a seven-match losing streak with a 32-22 victory over Castleford Tigers. Bulls had dropped to the bottom of the Betfred Super League table with a lengthy winless run which stretched back to July 10, but they were 18-0 up by the 19 minute mark after early scores for Riley Dean, Connor Wynne and Caleb Aekins. Dan Russell and Waqa Blake added further tries before the break and whilst Tigers briefly railed, Ebon Scurr grabbed a sixth effort for the hosts after 52 minutes to keep alive Bulls' hopes of avoiding the wooden spoon ahead of next Thursday's season finale at 13th-placed York.
